title: Activation Geometry as a Formal Alignment Invariant: A Cross-Architecture Test

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests the universality assumption of ELK: that truth geometry is consistent across architectures. If it is architecture-specific, ELK probes cannot transfer, which is a critical limitation for practical deployment of ELK-based oversight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training three small architectures on binary classification is feasible. PCA and UMAP on activations are well-supported by standard libraries. The misleading-label setup requires some care. Medium compute is sufficient for small models. Beginners can handle this with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three architectures, activation extraction, dimensionality reduction, geometric comparison. Each architecture is a training run, and comparing geometries across all three is analytical work. Tight but possible in 30 hours if architectures are small.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
